item.title: Microsoft Ends Copilot Support on LG and Samsung Smart TVs
item.description:
Microsoft Ends Copilot Support on LG and Samsung Smart TVs

Microsoft announced that it will discontinue the Copilot AI assistant on all smart TVs, including the LG and Samsung models that launched with the feature at CES 2025.

🔍 Overview

  • Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs.
  • The decision affects LG and Samsung TVs that received Copilot access in 2025.
  • The information originated from an on‑screen notification on a webOS‑powered LG TV, not from an official press release.

🗓️ Timeline

  • CES 2025: LG and Samsung announced new smart TVs with built‑in Microsoft Copilot.
  • December 2025: LG added an unremovable Copilot shortcut to its webOS, prompting user backlash.
  • Early 2026: LG allowed the shortcut to be deleted after user complaints.
  • 2026 (scheduled): Copilot functionality is slated for discontinuation on all TVs; the exact date is “subject to Microsoft’s timeline.”

🤖 What Copilot Did on TVs

  • Acted as an AI‑powered companion that users could chat with.
  • Answered questions about the current screen content.
  • Provided recommendations for TV shows and movies.

⚙️ Why the Change

  • Earlier in 2026, Microsoft launched a new Copilot “super app” that bundles chat, agents, and coding tools.
  • The super app shifts Copilot’s focus toward business and productivity uses rather than a digital companion on consumer devices.

📣 Current Status

  • A notification on LG TVs states: “the Copilot‑enabled feature on your TV is no longer available and may stop functioning shortly.”
  • No exact shutdown date has been provided; the feature is scheduled for discontinuation during 2026.

The discontinuation marks the end of the first generation of AI assistants embedded in mainstream smart TV platforms.

#Microsoft #Copilot #SmartTV #AI

Source: Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs

item.title: Google launches AI Edge Foresight, an offline‑only note‑taking app for macOS
item.description:
Google launches AI Edge Foresight, an offline‑only note‑taking app for macOS

Google has released an experimental note‑taking app called Google AI Edge Foresight that can transcribe meetings and audio files entirely offline.

🔍 Overview

  • Experimental app, free to use
  • Runs on macOS using Google’s on‑device EmbeddingGemma 2 model
  • Transcribes meetings completely offline

🧩 How it works

  • Audio is processed by an on‑device model; no cloud connection is required
  • The model runs locally on Macs with Apple Silicon

⚙️ Features

  • Offline transcription of meetings and audio files
  • Summarizes meetings while providing a space for personal notes, similar to Granola and Wispr Flow
  • Turns shorthand bullet points entered during a meeting into polished notes based on the transcript
  • Built‑in assistant lets you ask questions about the content you heard
  • Ability to connect local files for the assistant to reference when answering questions
  • Files, meeting audio, and notes never leave your computer

🚀 Availability

  • Free to use
  • Optimized for macOS on Apple Silicon Macs only

💡 Why it matters

  • Operates entirely on‑device, keeping data private
  • Provides a privacy‑focused alternative in the growing AI note‑taking market

#Google #AI #NoteTaking #macOS #Privacy

Source: Google’s AI note-taking app transcribes your meetings completely offline
